ordered_diagnoses: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with cerebrovascular involvement
salient_findings: Lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities on MRI
Multiple cerebral microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted imaging
key_facts: 2-year history of headache, dizziness, and imbalance
History of hypertension
History of cervical disc herniation
Underwent transcatheter closure for patent foramen ovale
Family history of progressive cognitive decline and imbalance
Father died of cerebral hemorrhage at age 65
Neurological examination revealed brisk bilateral tendon reflexes
Bilateral Babinski sign present
MRI showed lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities
Susceptibility-weighted imaging showed multiple cerebral microbleeds
Heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene, along with the patient's symptoms of headache, dizziness, and imbalance, and the imaging findings of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities, are consistent with CARASIL Syndrome, which is caused by mutations in the HTRA1 gene and typically presents with these features.

rejected.label: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)
rejected.why: CADASIL is typically associated with NOTCH3 gene mutations, not HTRA1 gene mutations.

rejected.label: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of dementia symptoms make this diagnosis less likely, and the imaging findings do not specifically suggest amyloid angiopathy.

rejected.label: Hypertensive Vasculopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of hypertension, the presence of a genetic mutation and specific imaging findings suggest a more specific diagnosis than hypertensive vasculopathy.

rejected.label: Col4A1-related disorder
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the vignette to suggest a Col4A1-related disorder, such as a family history of the condition or specific imaging findings consistent with it.
